solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keep tabs on screen

definitions.meaning: to keep tabs on someone is to watch or check them regularly
a computer's display unit, the device you look at

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: as a verb it means observe closely, and as a noun it is the display unit of a computer.

clue.text: A posh young lady once returned to get tucked up

indicators.note: returned means the word for the young lady is read backwards, going up the down light

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, was an upper-class girl formally presented to society, a custom now gone

explanation.surface: An old-style society girl comes back home and is put to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the society girl backwards, going up the down light; 'once' marks debutantes as a custom of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tucked up is snug in bed, which is the old adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Eccentric wanting party underneath waterfall

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece underneath another is written after it

parts.note: a weir is a low dam over which a river falls
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An odd character skips the party held below the waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underneath' puts DO below WEIR in this down light. 'wanting' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: an eccentric is an odd, strange person.

clue.text: Annoying hospital, wanting a second dressing for arm

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, seen on road signs
a sling is a bandage that supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: An irritating hospital stay where you wait for a second arm bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassling means pestering or bothering someone, and the clue's participle 'annoying' has the same sense.

clue.text: Get atlas out crossing motorway, seeing pillar pointing up

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters span the motorway, holding it inside them
out suggests the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A driver pulls out the atlas to cross the motorway and spots a tall column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GET ATLAS into STALAGTE, and 'crossing' puts MI (the M1, the London to Yorkshire motorway) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is a mineral column that rises from a cave floor, so it is a pillar pointing upward.

clue.text: One refusal covers idiot's vacuity

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: covers means the refusal word goes round the idiot word, hiding it inside

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
a nit is an informal word for a fool; the 's is only a link

explanation.surface: A single refusal hides a fool's emptiness of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts the idiot inside the refusal, between its A and Y, making NANITY; 'One' as I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanity is pointless silliness, the emptiness of thought that vacuity names.

clue.text: Something to wear two times?

parts.note: two of something is a double
T is the abbreviation for time; the clue's plural times means two T's, the double T

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what garment you might wear twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two times' reads as DOUBLE T, a pair of T's.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times, so it is clothing.

clue.text: Going without a bite after onset of fever

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the first letter
the onset of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: an insect's bite can be a sting

explanation.surface: Having nothing to eat after an insect bite brings on a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting is abstaining from food, so the person is going without.

clue.text: Amends made for poverty, with right to replace leader

indicators.note: to replace leader means the first letter of the poverty word is swapped for a new one

parts.note: destitution is extreme poverty

explanation.surface: Compensation is paid for the poor, with an entitlement swapped for a chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace leader' swaps the D at the front of DESTITUTION for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Restitution is compensation for a wrong, the act of making amends.

clue.text: Drew in less developed area of desolation

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An artist sketched in a less built-up part of a bleak region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' looks like a name or a sketch, but its letters are fodder with IN LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is a wild, uninhabited stretch of land, a desolate area.

clue.text: Slow very nearly becomes fast

indicators.note: very nearly means the musical term is used without its last letter

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slow

explanation.surface: Something slow almost turns into something quick, a paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very nearly' drops the final O of LENTO, the Italian tempo marking. 'fast' is not speed here but a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is the forty-day Christian season of fasting before Easter, so it is a fast.

clue.text: Oppose working during cold weather feature

indicators.note: during means the working word sits within the weather term

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, found on taps
a front is a boundary between air masses on a weather map
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Battling on through a cold front in the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places the working word between the cold letter and the weather feature, so the pieces read in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront someone is to face them in defiance, to oppose them.

clue.text: Time of year for pastime requiring punctuation and space?

definitions.text: Time of year for pastime requiring punctuation and space?

parts.words: Time of year for pastime requiring punctuation and space?
parts.note: pastime, given an apostrophe and a space, becomes pa's time, a day belonging to dad on the calendar

explanation.surface: A question about when a hobby needs commas and gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pastime' with an apostrophe and space reads 'pa's time', a day for dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint at the annual day honouring fathers, held in June in Britain and the US.

clue.text: Acquired rights, finally, on popular bars

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the earlier pieces are attached after the popular word

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
got means obtained or acquired

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Gaining rights at last to fashionable bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' is not pubs but blocks of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingots are cast blocks of gold or other metal, commonly called bars.

clue.text: Potentially make a profit from Roman gear pinched by substitute

indicators.note: pinched by means the Roman garment is held tightly within the substitute word

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute or understudy
a toga was the loose robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman costume stolen by an understudy might earn some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' looks like theft, but it signals that the Roman robe is held inside the substitute, splitting it after its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are likely to gain from something, you are in a position to profit from it.

clue.text: Teachers incubate bird

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
to hatch eggs is to incubate them

explanation.surface: Teachers keep eggs warm for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks.

clue.text: The lower socioeconomic groups took part in election, getting committed

parts.note: in British social grading, D and E are the two lowest classes
to cast a ballot is to have voted

explanation.surface: Poorer people turned out at the polls and showed loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research ranks social classes A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so the lowest two are D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted and committed both describe someone loyal and dedicated.

clue.text: Done 'urt by method of delivery?

parts.note: over means done or finished
'urt is hurt with the h dropped; hurt means harm, and with the h dropped Cockney-style that is 'arm

explanation.surface: Someone gets hurt by the way a ball is bowled at them.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'urt signals dropping the H from HARM. 'delivery' is cricket bowling, not post.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and other sports, an arm swung above the shoulder is a style of bowling or throwing.

clue.text: Leave day before tree's destroyed

indicators.note: before places the day letter in front of what follows
destroyed means the letters of the tree word are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the clue's tree's is read as trees, giving the letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: A day before a tree is cut down, someone departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges TREES (from 'tree's') into ESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon or leave a place or person.

clue.text: Do better than bodyguard for criminal overloaded with executive staff

parts.note: to top something is to surpass it
a heavy is a hired thug who protects a gangster

explanation.surface: Outdoing a gangster's minder.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation with too many senior managers relative to workers is described as top-heavy.

clue.text: Wordsworth lines? Yes

parts.note: William Wordsworth was an English Romantic poet
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: Asking whether Wordsworth wrote verse, and answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: Wordsworth's lines are verse, and 'Yes' confirms it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse written by Wordsworth is exactly what the clue describes, since his lines were poems.

clue.text: Beer bellies may give you piles

definitions.meaning: a pot, or pot belly, is a protruding stomach from drinking
... of money means large amounts, piles of it

explanation.definitionFit: Pots are paunches, and pots of cash are lots of it, matching piles.

clue.text: Honest sailor loves naked company administrators

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: naked means the word is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: the board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: A sailor loves exposing the company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips L and S from 'loves', leaving OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above board is open and legitimate, so it is honest.

clue.text: Love city and kiss stone!

parts.note: love in tennis scoring is nil, written O
NY is New York City
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to love a city and kiss a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Coppers must welcome a new act of atonement

indicators.note: must welcome means the coin word takes in the other letters

parts.note: coppers are low-value bronze coins, pennies or pence

explanation.surface: Police officers have to greet a fresh act of making amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but means pence, Britain's copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is a voluntary self-punishment to make up for sin, an act of atonement.

clue.text: Collects people who stump up to cross river

indicators.note: to cross means the payers word reaches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to stump up is British slang for to pay, so those who stump up are payers

explanation.surface: Debt collectors and people who pay up have to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collects' is not gathering but the noun: a collect is a short prayer in Anglican worship.
explanation.definitionFit: In church liturgy a collect is a short set prayer, so collects are prayers.
